Each of these layers requires innovations in hardware and software. A modular design of the hardware and software will be necessary to allow straightforward integration of new capabilities into the new imaging, visualization and estimation framework. Research in each layer can progress largely independently, though some integration effort will be necessary to test new methods in conjunction with the other capabilities of the new SDF platform. • Platform: This part of the SDF capability consists of the mobile platform (e.g., a UAV or UGV) as well as the software that embodies capabilities of path-planning, navigation and control, collision avoidance as well as the imaging locations (or trajectory) that allow the collection of the most informative measurements. This, in turn, implies the existence of a control system that uses the source reconstruction (and it uncertainty quantification) to identify the locations where measurements should be obtained. This control system can be quite complicated, especially if the SDF capability has to search of sources of radiation [8]. • Instrumentation: This layer is self-explanatory. It consists of the various sensors, lidar etc. that acquire measurements, and the associated software that is required to reconstruct the source (or the surrounding context). Uncertainty quantification, from each sensing modality, is also performed in the associated software. To date, the computational capabilities carried on the mobile platform have sufficed to perform the image reconstruction from data or the data was processed offline, reducing the need for telemetry, but use cases where telemetry on cloud-based analyses may be important in the future. Classification of geometries and surfaces inthecontextsurroundingtheradiationsource, representedasapointcloudcollectedbylidar, also belong to this layer [73, 74]. • Visualization: This layer concerns the visualization of the image reconstruction from the individual sensing modalities, for both the context and the radiation source. This is currently performed on a handheld tablet, which can also display the labels from the classification task performed on lidar measurements. Since this involves telemetry of data to an observer (and also might include the relay of instructions to the SDF platform) data compression research belongs to this layer (See Fig. 4). • Statistical inference & learning: This layer is devoted to the fusion of multimodal data, with the express aim of (1) obtaining quantitative (and perhaps spectroscopic) reconstruction of the radiation source, (2) ensuring sufficient data was collected when online processing is untenable; and/or (3) performing model selection and hyperparameter optimization in order to best determine the nature of the source. This is the most complex part of the reconstruction process, as each fusion technique will be specific to the modalities being fused and the goals/needs of the specific application. In addition, reconstructions with uncertainty quantification, especially when multimodal measurements reduce uncertainty, are performed here. Such complex computations will either require significant onboard computational power and specialized software design and implementation to execute on modern GPGPU architectures [57, 75], or will leverage more capable remote computational resources.
